topic: Analysis plan: objective, hypothesis, three PM tests
idea: Preliminary Analysis Plan = study objective (50-75 words answering: problem, alternatives and hypotheses, decision makers), key performance measures, scope, approach, Methods and Assumptions log, resources. A performance measure is kept only if it (1) can be observed in field data, (2) can be produced from simulation output, (3) can differentiate the alternatives; keep few measures because effort grows exponentially with their number.
does: Validate a note_plan: objective states problem+alternatives+hypothesis, 1-3 KPIs each answering the three questions (observable / produced by ACMS / discriminating), assumptions logged; refuse or warn on missing parts.
outputs: checklist with warnings (too many KPIs, KPI not produced by ACMS, no hypothesis)
existing: partial: note_plan (goal, hypothesis, plan, expectation, conclusion)
cite: Ch 1 Establish Project Purpose, Select Key Performance Measures, Preliminary Analysis Plan
notes: Also a Methods and Assumptions log kept across the conversation.

topic: Scope must encompass all congestion; extend boundary if queues reach it
idea: Model geography and time horizon must cover all congestion caused by the alternatives and adjacent areas affected by diversion; if queues appear in boundary areas extend the network upstream or lengthen the time horizon, or post-process to estimate the missing congestion.
does: After a run, flag queues or blocked insertion at boundary ends (spawn backlog, queue length reaching the end) and a run horizon too short to clear congestion (vehicles still queued at the end), saying the result is truncated.
outputs: flags: boundary queue, end-of-run backlog, horizon too short
cite: Ch 1 Define Scope
notes: Related to diagnose_run_health; unserved demand at the end of a run biases mean trip time low.

topic: Where microsimulation is warranted
idea: Use microsimulation for lane-level capacity and throughput effects, time-dynamic onset/intensity/duration of congestion, and multi-facility congestion spillback; otherwise use less data-intensive tools (HCM, macroscopic).
does: Assistant guidance mapping a question to ACMS capability and its limits.
outputs: advice
cite: Ch 1 Develop the Analytical Approach

topic: Seven-step process with documented methods and assumptions
idea: Planning, data collection and analysis, base model, error checking, calibration, alternatives analysis, final report; calibration must be accepted before alternatives analysis starts; stakeholder review at milestones.
does: Enforce an order in the assistant: check design (error check) then calibrate then experiment then report, refusing run_experiment conclusions on an uncalibrated model without saying so.
outputs: warnings
cite: Introduction, Fig 1

topic: Compare alternatives within each travel condition
idea: Average over all days confounds: an adaptive signal strategy may look bad because the post period had severe weather. Group days by travel condition (clusters of demand, weather, incidents, throughput, travel time) and compare alternatives within each condition; run one calibrated model variant per condition.
does: run_experiment variant that repeats every scenario under a few named stress conditions (demand level, a lane-blocking incident, reduced speed for weather) from cluster_conditions and reports which alternative wins under which condition.
inputs: scenarios, conditions (demand scale, incident schedule, speed factor), seeds
outputs: matrix scenario x condition of paired differences and winner per condition
existing: partial: cluster_conditions, run_experiment (demand scaling only), schedule_emergency
cite: Ch 2 intro (travel conditions), Ch 5, Ch 6
notes: ACMS cannot yet inject incidents or weather into an experiment scenario; condition = demand scale, incident (blocked lane for t min), weather (speed/headway factor). Adds the missing 'when does it work' answer.

topic: Count consistency check before calibration
idea: Reconcile counts: upstream vs downstream counts should agree; investigate differences above 10% where no source/sink (driveway) lies between; counts at 15-minute resolution, starting before congestion and ending after it clears so they measure demand not capacity; use control-station counts to adjust counts taken on different days; counts and demand data must be contemporaneous.
does: Before calibrate_demand/check_calibration, test the supplied counts: flag pairs of consecutive roads with more than 10% flow difference and no junction source or sink, counts at a congested location (flow below capacity-implied), and mixed dates.
outputs: list of inconsistent count pairs with % difference
cite: Ch 2 Demand Data, Verify Data Quality
notes: Counts on a congested link measure capacity, not demand: warn.

topic: Calibration measure set: localized plus system
idea: Calibrate to at least two measures: one localized (bottleneck throughput or duration, density, queue extent, stops, intersection delay, turning percentages) and one system (travel time or speed profile, travel time index, planning index, travel time variance); bottleneck throughput measured within 0.5 mile upstream or immediately downstream of the bottleneck; at least one stationary bottleneck identified; travel times for paths that intersect a bottleneck at 15-minute intervals.
does: check_calibration reports whether the supplied field data cover at least one localized and one system measure and says what is missing; suggests the bottleneck from the run (max flow-drop point) to place a detector.
outputs: coverage report, suggested bottleneck links
cite: Ch 2 Bottleneck Throughput, Travel Time, Data for Calibration
notes: Bottleneck detection from the run: link with highest sustained discharge flow downstream of a queue.

topic: Travel-condition attribute processing
idea: Cluster inputs: map qualitative attributes (incident type x lanes blocked) to a numeric severity index covering all observed combinations (Table 2, 13 levels), do not bin numeric data, normalise x' = a + (x - xmin)(b - a)/(xmax - xmin) (Eq 1), drop attributes highly correlated with each other (keep the one most correlated with the key measure; PCA optional), include time-variant travel time and bottleneck throughput as attributes; stopping heuristic k from 3 to 2*sqrt(n/2) minimising within/between variance (Eq 2) or normalised CV x normalised k (Eq 3).
does: Improve cluster_conditions: attribute correlation screening, severity-index helper for categorical incidents, Eq 3 stopping criterion, weighted multiple key measures.
outputs: cleaned attributes, chosen k and criterion
cite: Ch 2 Cluster analysis steps 1-6
notes: ACMS already follows this; extras are correlation screening and Eq 3.

topic: Staged error-checking protocol before calibration
idea: Error checking: (1) input checklist (connectivity, link length/lanes/speed/type, control type and data, prohibited turns, vehicle mix per entry, sources and sinks, zone volumes vs counts, turn percentages, OD of trips); (2) run at extremely low demand, trace single vehicles and flag any unexpected slowdown or stop, repeat for several OD pairs; (3) run at 50 percent of demand, which should not congest, and check entry and exit flows equal (all demand loaded); (4) simple test problems (single link or intersection) whose capacity or speed can be computed by hand; key decision point before calibration.
does: Automatic headless checks: free-flow run at tiny demand listing vehicles whose mean speed falls below a fraction of the limit and where (stop/slow locations), a 50% demand run reporting congestion and any entry/exit flow mismatch, and design-consistency flags (speed discontinuities along a route, stacked nodes, vehicle mix not summing to 100%).
outputs: report: anomalies by location, flow balance table, pass/fail gate
cite: Ch 4 Review Input Errors, View Animation, Residual Errors
notes: Low-demand slow-point detection is a direct bug-finder for the simulator itself (e.g. odd junction geometry). Reuse run_simulation and per-vehicle trace.

topic: Simulation period includes loading and clearing time
idea: Simulate analysis period plus time for network loading and congestion build-up before and congestion dissipation after (analysis 6-9 AM, simulate 5-10 AM); extra time set by looking at data; data collection also spans this.
does: Experiments and run_simulation take warm-up and clear-out minutes, report KPIs only over the analysis window, and warn when vehicles remain on the road at the end or when the window starts empty.
outputs: KPIs over window, truncation warning
cite: Ch 3 Simulation Run Control Data
notes: Check whether ACMS KPIs include the empty-network start.

topic: Seed instability as a model-error signal
idea: Variation from random seeds is markedly lower than variation from travel conditions; if significant variation appears between seeds, suspect coding errors or gridlock (unresolved contention such as conflicting parallel lane changes); results from an unstable model must not be used for calibration or alternatives analysis. Calibrate a single run per condition, not many seeds.
does: In run_experiment output, flag a scenario whose across-seed CV of a headline KPI exceeds a threshold or whose runs include gridlock/deadlock, and mark its differences 'unreliable'.
outputs: stability flag per scenario with CV and deadlock count
cite: Ch 5 Overview of the Calibration Process

topic: Representative day selection (Eq 5-7)
idea: For each travel condition choose the single observed day closest to the cluster mean: m-bar(t,j) = sum_i m_ij(t)/N (Eq 5); relative deviation m-dot_ij(t) = sqrt((mbar - m_ij(t))^2)/mbar (Eq 6); i* = argmin_i sum_m sum_j sum_t m-dot (Eq 7). Calibrate to that one real day, never to an averaged synthetic day (averages smooth incidents into conditions that never occurred).
does: Extend cluster_conditions to return the representative day of each cluster by Eq 5-7 over time-variant 15-minute series.
inputs: days with 15-min series of key measures per route/location
outputs: representative day per cluster
cite: Ch 5 Identify Representative Days, Eq 5-7
notes: Check if cluster_conditions already returns it; ACMS docs may cover Eq 5-7.

topic: Bottleneck onset and duration measure
idea: Bottleneck: location where demand exceeds capacity and approach speed falls below a congestion speed threshold (rule of thumb one third of free-flow speed, applied uniformly); onset = 15-minute period when the upstream location first has speed below the threshold; duration = time until average speed exceeds the threshold again; use mean space speed when upstream of a signal.
does: KPI per link from a run: congestion onset time, duration and peak discharge flow, using the one-third free-flow threshold, and a ranked bottleneck list; also a match score against observed onset/duration in check_calibration.
inputs: run (link speeds by 15 min), free-flow speed
outputs: bottleneck table: link, onset, duration, discharge veh/h
existing: partial: analyse_run (95th percentile queue vs length), read_detectors, critical_links
cite: Ch 5 Bottleneck measures, Congestion speed threshold, onset, duration
notes: Gives the localized calibration measure that FHWA requires beside travel time; also explains where an alternative helps.

topic: Sensitivity testing of uncertain inputs
idea: After the alternatives comparison, rerun with changed demand levels and uncertain assumptions (e.g. share of drivers using traveller information, forecast demand) to test whether the conclusion is robust; demand sensitivity especially for future years since forecasts are less precise than the model.
does: Take a finished experiment and vary chosen inputs (demand scale, a parameter such as bus share, signal compliance, incident rate) over a grid and report whether the ranking and the 'clear' verdicts of the scenarios hold at each level.
outputs: verdict stability table: winner and significance per level, break-even level where ranking flips
existing: partial: run_experiment (demand scaling to stress), scale_demand, regress (demand_scale as regressor)
cite: Ch 6 Perform Sensitivity Testing, Forecast Future Demands
notes: The break-even demand level at which the preferred design stops winning is a useful decision statistic.

topic: Frequency-weighted aggregate over travel conditions
idea: Combine alternative results across travel conditions with weights n_i = days in each cluster: weighted mean x-bar_j = sum(x_i n_i)/sum(n_i) (Eq 21); percentile measures (95th percentile planning time index) from the pooled results; variance across clusters (Eq 22); then pooled-variance t-test, H0 mu1 >= mu2 one-sided (Eq 23-24) with an example (PTI 1.85 vs 2.65, t = -5.48).
does: experiment_by_condition output also a single frequency-weighted result per scenario, and pooled PTI, with the one-sided test.
outputs: weighted KPI and significance per scenario
cite: Ch 6 Perform Hypothesis Testing, Eq 21-24, Table 13
notes: Needs travel conditions with frequencies (days per year in each cluster) from cluster_conditions.

topic: Replication count with tolerance floor from observed variation
idea: Tolerance error e is computed from the observed within-cluster variation at the two critical time intervals (e = t*s/(sqrt(n)*mean), Eq 17-19) with a floor of 5 percent; run the model 4 times first, N = (t3,95% s / (e xbar))^2 (Eq 20); take the maximum over all key measures and clusters; if N exceeds 20 investigate gridlock rather than replicating.
does: replications tool that takes the tolerance from observed field variability instead of a fixed precision, with a 5 percent floor, over all KPIs and conditions.
outputs: N runs, binding KPI
cite: Ch 6 Determine Required Number of Replications, Eq 15-20
notes: ACMS uses a user precision; only the field-derived tolerance and max over measures are new.

topic: Final report structure with Methods and Assumptions
idea: Final report: objectives and scope, approach with Methods and Assumptions entries, data, travel conditions, calibration tests and results, forecast assumptions, alternatives described by intent and model parameters, results, conclusions; a separate technical appendix with software version so another analyst can repeat it. Inform decision makers, do not decide for them; present a story, not all details.
does: AI Mode final report template fed by the planning journal: objective, assumptions log, calibration status, alternatives with parameters changed, results with significance, caveats.
outputs: structured report text
existing: partial: planning journal in experiment workbook (note_plan, tool calls)
cite: Ch 7

topic: Work zone scenario with timed lane closure
idea: Work zone modelled as capacity and speed impacts over a ~2000 ft (about 600 m) section: inactive (but present) zone = 5% capacity loss on all lanes and speed down 10 mph; active zone = one lane removed, 33% capacity drop per remaining lane (narrowed lanes) and speed down 20 mph. Schedule alternatives: fixed (never active in peaks) vs dynamic (active on low-demand days) with supporting measures (incident clearance time halved, 2% demand diverted to alternate modes and routes).
does: Scenario edit for run_experiment/build_scenario: a work zone on a road segment (start, length m, lanes closed, active window, speed drop, capacity factor per remaining lane) applied as a time-windowed lane closure and speed limit, plus a speed-and-capacity friction when inactive.
inputs: road id, offset and length (m), lanes closed, active hours, speed reduction, capacity factor
outputs: scenario with work zone
existing: partial: update_roads (lanes, speed), schedule_emergency; no timed partial-length closure
cite: Appendix A Work Zone Alternative Analysis
notes: Needs a segment-level lane block and speed zone in simulation.py; also useful for road-closure experiments seen in AgentSUMO and ChatSUMO.

topic: Incident injection and response time in scenarios
idea: Incident management alternative modelled as halving incident duration; demand management as reducing demand 2% on selected routes; incidents defined by time, location, type, lanes blocked, clearance time, and travel conditions clustered by incident count and maximum duration.
does: Scenario element: a blockage of N lanes on a road from time t for d minutes (clearance), with a stochastic incident generator by rate per vehicle-km, so experiments can test response measures (clear in half the time).
inputs: road, lanes blocked, start, duration or incident rate and duration distribution
outputs: scenario with incident process
cite: Appendix A alternatives; Ch 3 Event Data
notes: Enables reliability analysis (planning time index) under non-recurrent congestion, which FHWA treats as first-order.

topic: Average day vs travel conditions demonstration and total additional delay with monetisation
idea: With one averaged day the two alternatives could not be separated (delay 2,567,483 vs 2,588,419 h, t-test not significant); with travel conditions weighted by frequency (20,13,3,21,14,29 percent) Alternative 2 was significantly lower (1,992,057 vs 1,832,387 h). Cost compare: soft cost = delay hours x $20/h, plus hard costs (fixed, daily, set-up, management measures per day). Planning time index = 95th percentile travel time / free-flow travel time per interval.
does: Convert experiment results to a total cost: delay hours x value of time plus user-supplied hard costs per scenario, with the weighted-condition roll-up, so the assistant ranks alternatives by total cost and reliability.
inputs: experiment, value of time, hard costs per scenario, days of exposure
outputs: total cost table and PTI by scenario
cite: Appendix A Travel Conditions Alternatives Analysis, Total Cost Comparison, Table 18-20
notes: Value of time and costs are inputs; ACMS has no cost model. Delay hours scale by exposure days.
